hero.headline: Airlines face $100 billion fuel cost increase as oil prices surge
hero.body:
Global airlines are confronting an additional $100 billion in jet fuel costs this year following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz in March, which disrupted oil supplies during the conflict with Iran. The fuel shock has prompted the International Air Transport Association to slash profit forecasts, with collective industry profits expected to halve to $23 billion as jet fuel prices rise 70% across 2026.

The IATA gathered in Rio de Janeiro to address the mounting financial pressure on carriers worldwide, with fuel representing their single largest operating expense. Multiple carriers have already indicated that ticket price increases appear inevitable to offset the rising costs.

"High oil prices will inevitably mean higher ticket prices," said Willie Walsh, IATA's director general. "There's just no way to avoid that." Walsh acknowledged that industry polling showed passengers were now braced for higher fares and prepared to spend more, though he noted that how long travelers can tolerate the higher costs of connectivity remains uncertain.

Walsh described the situation as "a challenging and unpredictable time" with "wafer-thin margins," adding that "for a lot of airlines the increase in the fuel bill is potentially existential." However, he distinguished the current situation from previous crises, noting that concerns about fuel shortages had subsided and that the industry remained profitable overall with traffic up 2 percent.

Sean Doyle, chief executive of British Airways, acknowledged that fare increases were unavoidable, though he suggested they would affect different routes differently. Long-haul and business passengers would likely face the bulk of increases, while price-sensitive short-haul holiday flights would be the last to see higher fares, he said.

According to IATA research, approximately half of passengers indicated they were prepared to spend substantially more on fares if prices tracked oil costs, which Walsh said "bodes well" for a strong summer season. However, British and European travelers showed a preference for flying within the continent rather than venturing farther afield given uncertainty around Gulf hubs.

The airlines body also raised concerns about the EU's new entry-exit system, which requires biometric checks on most non-EU travelers. Rafael Schvartsman, IATA's vice-president for Europe, warned that the system could create substantial delays, with processing times potentially extending to 90 seconds per passenger rather than the current 20 to 25 seconds. He expressed particular concern about impacts on British travelers, who represent the largest number of tourists to Mediterranean destinations.

While Greece announced it would exempt UK nationals from the new checks, Schvartsman argued the issue affected many airports and could not be resolved through single-country exemptions, noting that American carriers were already adding extra European flights during summer months.

cards.headline: Iran launches missile barrage in latest strike on Israel
cards.teaser: Iran fired a barrage of missiles at Israel in its latest military strike, according to reports appearing on front pages across the UK.
cards.body:
Iran launched a missile barrage at Israel, marking the first attack since a fragile ceasefire began in early April. The strike threatens to complicate ongoing mediation efforts aimed at ending the war in the region.

The attack dominated front-page coverage across major newspapers on Monday, alongside reports of Danish footballer Christian Eriksen's on-field collapse.

cards.headline: Trump urges Netanyahu not to retaliate after Iranian missile strike
cards.teaser: President Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday not to retaliate against Iran's missile attack and to allow more time for diplomacy, ac.
cards.body:
President Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday not to retaliate against Iran's missile attack and to allow more time for diplomacy, according to a senior U.S. official and an Israeli source familiar with the call. The conversation took place after Iran launched ballistic missiles at northern Israel on Sunday night, the first such strike in two months.

Trump's intervention signals the administration's effort to prevent escalating tensions between Israel and Iran from undermining ongoing U.S. negotiations with Tehran. Before the call, Trump told reporters he planned to urge Netanyahu to hold off on any military response. A U.S. official confirmed that Trump has been briefed on the Iranian missile attack.

The missile strike threatened to derail a fragile ceasefire that had held between the U.S. and Iran. The Israeli Defense Forces posted about the attack on social media, confirming that Iran had launched ballistic missiles targeting northern Israel. The incident marked Tehran's first direct strike on Israel since the ceasefire took effect two months ago.

The Trump administration has been working to negotiate with Iran even as the U.S. remains engaged in military operations against the country. The president has faced criticism over his Iran policy, with some observers questioning whether the conflict contradicts his 2024 campaign promise of no new wars. Trump has rejected that characterization, dismissing suggestions that launching military action against Iran betrayed his campaign messaging.

The situation presents a diplomatic challenge for the administration as it attempts to balance its relationship with Israel, manage tensions with Iran, and advance negotiations. Former national security adviser John Bolton warned in an opinion piece that Trump's actions in the conflict with Iran could spark a nuclear arms race in the Middle East, regardless of any eventual deal. The administration now faces the task of preventing further escalation while continuing diplomatic efforts with Tehran.

cards.headline: Ukraine Seeks European Mediation as US Steps Back from Peace Talks
cards.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelensky met with leaders of Britain, Germany and France in London to discuss potential negotiators for talks with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with the leaders of Britain, Germany and France in London to propose that these European nations serve as mediators in potential peace negotiations with Russia. The meeting reflects a strategic shift as US President Donald Trump's diplomatic focus turns toward the conflict with Iran.

During the discussions, Zelensky's European allies outlined five conditions for entering peace talks with Moscow. This move signals Ukraine's effort to secure alternative diplomatic channels as American involvement in the peace process diminishes.

cards.headline: European Allies Set Five Conditions for Ukraine Peace Talks
cards.teaser: Britain, Germany and France outlined requirements for entering negotiations as US focus shifts to Iran conflict.
cards.body:
President Zelensky met with leaders from Britain, Germany, and France in London to discuss peace negotiations with Russia. The three European nations outlined five conditions for their participation in talks, positioning themselves as potential negotiators in the conflict.

The meeting reflects a shift in international dynamics as U.S. President Donald Trump's diplomatic focus turns toward Iran. Ukraine is increasingly looking to its European allies to play a central role in shaping any settlement discussions.

cards.headline: Bolton warns Trump's Iran policy risks nuclear proliferation
cards.teaser: Former national security adviser says administration decisions during conflict have laid groundwork for arms race.
cards.body:
Former national security adviser John Bolton warned Sunday that President Trump's actions in the war against Iran could spark a nuclear arms race in the Middle East. Bolton made the assessment in an opinion piece published Sunday.

Bolton argued that regardless of any deal Trump reaches with Iran, the president's decisions during the conflict have created conditions for increased nuclear proliferation in the region. He characterized Trump's approach as contradictory and warned of long-term consequences for regional security.

cards.headline: OPEC+ raises oil output quota for fourth time since Hormuz closure
cards.teaser: The oil cartel approved another production increase as global energy markets respond to Middle East supply disruptions.
cards.body:
OPEC and its allies approved a fourth increase to oil output quotas following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The move represents the latest attempt by major oil-producing nations to manage global supply amid ongoing disruptions to energy flows through the critical shipping channel.

The production increases come as oil prices have climbed in recent trading sessions, with markets reacting to military strikes and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The Strait of Hormuz closure has forced tankers to use longer alternative routes, adding costs and time to oil shipments reaching global markets.

hero.headline: Ukraine Seeks European Mediation as US Steps Back from Peace Talks
hero.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelensky met with leaders of Britain, Germany and France in London to discuss potential negotiators for talks with Russia.
hero.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with the leaders of Britain, Germany and France in London to propose that these European nations serve as mediators in potential peace negotiations with Russia. The meeting reflects a strategic shift as US President Donald Trump's diplomatic focus turns toward the conflict with Iran.

During the discussions, Zelensky's European allies outlined five conditions for entering peace talks with Moscow. This move signals Ukraine's effort to secure alternative diplomatic channels as American involvement in the peace process diminishes.

cards.headline: Peru Presidential Runoff Too Close to Call, Exit Polls Show
cards.teaser: Exit polls from Peru's presidential election runoff show no clear winner between the two candidates.
cards.body:
Peru's presidential runoff election between Keiko Fujimori and leftist congressman Roberto Sánchez proved too close to call based on exit polls. The race represents a stark left-right choice for voters, with Fujimori, daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori, facing off against Sánchez, a former trade and tourism minister.

The election outcome will determine who becomes Peru's ninth president in a decade. Voters prioritized stability and addressing the country's mounting challenges, including rising crime and inequality. The runoff reflects deep political polarization, mirroring the ideological divide that defined Peru's 2021 presidential election.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping Plans Visit to North Korea
cards.teaser: Beijing aims to reassert influence over North Korea as the strategic partnership faces new complexities.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping is visiting North Korea for a two-day trip, his first in nearly seven years. He is expected to meet with North Korea's leader, Kim Jong-un, in Pyongyang as China seeks to revitalise its relationship with its only formal treaty ally.

The China-North Korea relationship has weakened in recent years due to a sharp drop in trade during the Covid-19 pandemic and Pyongyang's increasingly close ties with Russia. Xi's visit represents Beijing's effort to reassert influence over the strategically important nation.

cards.headline: European Allies Set Five Conditions for Ukraine Peace Talks
cards.teaser: Britain, Germany and France outlined requirements for entering negotiations as US focus shifts to Iran conflict.
cards.body:
President Zelensky met with leaders from Britain, Germany, and France in London to discuss peace negotiations with Russia. The three European nations outlined five conditions for their participation in talks, positioning themselves as potential negotiators in the conflict.

The meeting reflects a shift in international dynamics as U.S. President Donald Trump's diplomatic focus turns toward Iran. Ukraine is increasingly looking to its European allies to play a central role in shaping any settlement discussions.

cards.headline: Senegal President and Prime Minister in Public Rift
cards.teaser: The two leaders who defeated Senegal's political establishment are now fighting each other.
cards.body:
A bitter public dispute has erupted between Senegal's president and prime minister, two men who rose to power together by defeating the country's political establishment. The conflict threatens to destabilize the West African nation's government and undermine the reform agenda that brought them to office.

The rift marks a dramatic reversal for the partnership that promised to bring change to Senegalese politics. The dispute highlights the challenges of maintaining political coalitions after electoral victory and raises questions about the stability of Senegal's government as internal divisions deepen.

cards.headline: Iran Rejects Using Its Assets to Pay Damages to US Allies
cards.teaser: Tehran dismissed American proposals to redirect frozen Iranian assets to Gulf states for reconstruction costs.
cards.body:
Iran has rejected a U.S. proposal to use frozen Iranian assets to compensate Gulf allies for damages from regional conflicts. The Treasury Department had considered the plan as a means for Gulf nations to recover reconstruction costs.

Iran's government views the proposal as an improper seizure of sovereign assets. The disagreement heightens tensions between Iran and the United States amid ongoing military confrontations between Iran and Israel.

cards.headline: Spain Tourism Reaches Record Highs as Visitors Avoid Middle East
cards.teaser: The country welcomed 9.1 million international visitors in April, the highest ever for that month.
cards.body:
Spain recorded 9.1 million international visitors in April, the highest number ever for that month. The surge in tourism reflects a shift in travel patterns as visitors seek alternatives to Middle East destinations amid regional tensions and security concerns.

The influx of tourists provides an economic boost to Spain as other Mediterranean and Middle Eastern destinations experience declining visitor numbers. The data demonstrates how geopolitical instability can redirect global travel flows toward European destinations perceived as safer alternatives.

hero.headline: Travel bans and visa restrictions leave World Cup fans unable to attend U.S. tournament
hero.body:
Fans from around the world are expressing frustration that U.S. travel restrictions and visa requirements are preventing them from attending the 2026 World Cup, with many feeling excluded from a tournament designed to celebrate global sport.

The restrictions affect potential attendees from multiple countries who face either outright travel bans or challenging visa application processes. The complaints arrive as the United States prepares to co-host the tournament with Canada and Mexico, marking the first World Cup held on American soil since 1994.

The tension between U.S. immigration policy and the demands of hosting a global sporting event has become increasingly apparent. World Cup tournaments typically attract hundreds of thousands of international visitors over several weeks, requiring host nations to accommodate massive numbers of short-term travelers from all countries. The current U.S. travel framework was not originally designed to manage such a large influx.

FIFA, soccer's international governing body, has not publicly stated whether it is working with U.S. authorities to establish temporary visa pathways or exemptions for ticketed fans. Other World Cup host nations have previously streamlined their processes by implementing temporary visa waivers or simplified application procedures to ensure fans could attend matches. It remains uncertain what measures the U.S. will implement.

The access challenges complicate an already complex logistical undertaking. The 2026 World Cup will be the first to feature 48 teams, an expansion from the traditional 32-team format, and matches will be distributed across cities in three countries across multiple time zones. The tournament is projected to generate billions in economic activity, but achieving those figures depends significantly on international visitors being able to enter the country.

Emma Hayes, writing about the tournament's scope, notes the geographical challenges involved. She describes how vast North America is, emphasizing that the land mass of England could fit comfortably into Georgia alone. With 104 matches scheduled across 16 venues spanning three time zones, traveling between games will be taxing for fans already facing high ticket prices.

The scale of the tournament presents unprecedented challenges. Teams will need to adjust to extensive travel between matches played thousands of miles apart in different countries. Fans planning to follow their national teams will encounter similar complications, potentially discouraging attendance.

The combination of travel restrictions, visa difficulties, and the tournament's logistical demands has created barriers that may limit the international attendance the event typically generates. This raises concerns about whether the World Cup, promoted as a celebration of global sport, will be equally accessible to fans worldwide or whether immigration policies and geography will determine who can participate in this historic tournament.

cards.headline: Flight attendant found dead on Florida beach after being struck by boat
cards.teaser: The body of a 31-year-old American Airlines flight attendant was found on a Hollywood Beach after she was hit by a vessel while snorkeling.
cards.body:
The body of a 31-year-old woman was discovered washed ashore on Hollywood Beach in Florida. Authorities identified her as an American Airlines flight attendant from California. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission determined she had been struck by a boat.

The woman had been snorkeling off a state park in Broward County when the incident occurred. Fishermen discovered her body on the beach. The investigation into the circumstances of the boat strike is ongoing.

cards.headline: Teen hiker dies from heat-related illness on Grand Canyon trail
cards.teaser: An 18-year-old hiker died after showing symptoms of heat-related illness on a strenuous trail through Grand Canyon National Park.
cards.body:
An 18-year-old hiker died at Grand Canyon National Park after experiencing heat-related illness while on the Bright Angel Trail. The teen showed symptoms of heat distress during the strenuous hike through the canyon, prompting park officials to respond to a distress call.

The death highlights the dangers hikers face at the Grand Canyon, where heat-related incidents occur regularly. Temperatures can reach dangerous levels, particularly during summer months and on trails that descend into the canyon.

cards.headline: Trump ends NBC interview after being challenged on election claims
cards.teaser: President Trump abruptly walked out of a Meet the Press interview after the host pressed him on false claims about the 2024 election.
cards.body:
President Trump abruptly ended an NBC "Meet the Press" interview after clashing with host Kristen Welker over his claims that the election was rigged. The president was repeatedly challenged on the accuracy of his statements during the taping.

The interview was cut short before its scheduled conclusion when Trump walked out following the confrontation about his election fraud assertions.

cards.headline: Trump defends Iran war against criticism of campaign promises
cards.teaser: President Trump rejected the notion that launching a war with Iran contradicts his 2024 campaign pledge of no new wars.
cards.body:
President Trump dismissed criticism that the war with Iran violates his campaign message. During his 2024 White House run, Trump repeatedly promised no new wars as a central theme of his foreign policy platform.

The president is now defending the decision to go to war with Iran despite that earlier pledge. The conflict represents a major military engagement that some observers say contradicts the campaign rhetoric Trump used to win election.

cards.headline: Chinese President Xi Jinping visits North Korea amid questions about Beijing's influence
cards.teaser: Xi Jinping is traveling to North Korea as China seeks to reassert influence over a strategically important but unpredictable partner.
cards.body:
Chinese President Xi Jinping is visiting North Korea for two days, his first trip there in nearly seven years. He is expected to meet with North Korea's leader Kim Jong-un in Pyongyang.

The visit aims to revitalize China-North Korea ties, which have deteriorated in recent years. Trade between the countries virtually froze during the Covid-19 pandemic, and North Korea has strengthened its relationship with Russia. Despite the strain, North Korea remains China's only formal treaty ally.

cards.headline: Air India crash survivors and witnesses describe lasting impact one year later
cards.teaser: A year after the Air India crash, people on the ground share how the disaster continues to affect their lives.
cards.body:
One year after an Air India crash, people on the ground are sharing how the disaster has affected them. Their accounts include those of a grandfather, a survivor, and a witness to the crash.

The psychological toll extends far beyond those who were aboard the aircraft. One survivor revealed that the trauma has fundamentally changed their relationship with everyday life, saying they no longer look at the sky. The crash has left lasting emotional and psychological scars on people in the area where the plane went down.

cards.body:
OPEC and its allies approved a fourth increase to oil output quotas following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The move represents the latest attempt by major oil-producing nations to manage global supply amid ongoing disruptions to energy flows through the critical shipping channel.

The production increases come as oil prices have climbed in recent trading sessions, with markets reacting to military strikes and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The Strait of Hormuz closure has forced tankers to use longer alternative routes, adding costs and time to oil shipments reaching global markets.

cards.headline: Stock futures decline as Middle East strikes rattle investors
cards.teaser: U.S. equity futures dropped following attacks in the region that threatened to undermine ceasefire efforts.
cards.body:
Stock futures declined in early trading following Iran's attack on Israel, rattling markets already weakened by a tech sector selloff. The geopolitical escalation threatened the stability of recent ceasefire efforts in the region.

Energy markets responded sharply, with oil prices jumping more than $2 per barrel amid concerns about potential supply disruptions. The combination of geopolitical tensions and ongoing tech weakness has left U.S. stock indexes under pressure.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO valuation under scrutiny after market downturn
cards.teaser: Investors question whether the company's $1.75 trillion target can hold after Friday's market selloff.
cards.body:
SpaceX is preparing for what's being called the biggest stock market launch in history, with shares set to release on June 12 at a $135 valuation per share. The company plans to sell 555.6 million shares, raising $75 billion from the offering.

Up to a quarter of the shares will be reserved for individual investors rather than institutional funds and banks—a significantly larger retail allocation than typical for major IPOs. This expanded access reflects efforts to broaden participation in the historic offering.

cards.headline: Trump criticizes potential Fed rate increases despite strong jobs report
cards.teaser: The president called for rate cuts and said there is no reason to raise interest rates after employment data exceeded expectations.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump said Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh should "do whatever he wants" while simultaneously criticizing the possibility of rate hikes ahead of Warsh's upcoming policy meeting. Trump argued against tightening monetary policy following a strong jobs report.

The stock market fell despite the positive employment data, prompting market analysis from Barclays. According to Barclays analysts, the economy is entering a warning zone, suggesting that robust job growth may signal economic stress rather than health. The situation highlights growing tension between the White House and the Federal Reserve over monetary policy direction.

cards.headline: Scary Movie reboot opens with $55 million at box office
cards.teaser: The R-rated comedy posted the biggest opening for its genre in 12 years.
cards.body:
The latest Scary Movie film earned $55 million during its opening weekend in the United States and Canada, securing the top position at the box office. This marks the largest debut for an R-rated comedy in over a decade.

The franchise's return comes as the spoof comedy takes aim at contemporary horror films and other targets. The film's performance demonstrates continued audience interest in the parody series, which has built its reputation on satirizing popular culture moments.

cards.headline: Marks & Spencer launches trainee program for 1,000 young people
cards.teaser: The British retailer aims to address the growing number of youth not in employment, education, or training.
cards.body:
Marks & Spencer has launched a new traineeship scheme for 1,000 young people. The program is designed to address what the retailer describes as a growing challenge: young people who are not in employment, education, or training.

The initiative aims to provide a pathway into careers within retail and related sectors, helping to tackle youth unemployment while meeting the company's own workforce needs.

hero.headline: Prada designs spacesuits for NASA's Artemis IV moon mission
hero.body:
Prada is expanding its reach into aerospace engineering through a collaboration with NASA to develop spacesuits for upcoming lunar missions. The luxury fashion house is working on specialized gear that astronauts will wear during the Artemis program's return to the moon.

The partnership focuses on creating the Liquid Cooling and Ventilation Garment (LCVG), which serves as the base layer worn underneath the main spacesuit. This undergarment plays a critical role in maintaining astronaut comfort and safety during lunar surface operations. The collaboration represents a notable shift for Prada, which is applying its expertise in advanced materials and manufacturing to space exploration technology.

NASA's Artemis program aims to return humans to the lunar surface for the first time since the Apollo missions ended in 1972. According to NASA's revised timeline, the Artemis IV mission is scheduled for 2028 and will include a lunar landing near the moon's south pole. The agency has adjusted its approach to the program, introducing additional test missions before attempting a crewed moon landing. This incremental strategy reflects recommendations from independent safety experts who raised concerns about the original plan's ambitious scope.

The revised Artemis schedule includes several steps before the 2028 landing. Artemis II, originally planned for March, has been rescheduled to launch no earlier than April. This mission will send four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon without landing. Technical issues, including a helium flow blockage and hydrogen leaks, prompted the delay and led NASA to return the rocket to its hangar for repairs.

NASA administrator Jared Isaacman explained the new approach as a return to tested methodology. The agency will conduct additional missions in low Earth orbit to test critical technologies before attempting the lunar landing, similar to how the original Apollo program included multiple crewed missions before the first moon landing in 1969. This staged approach allows engineers to identify and resolve technical challenges before proceeding to more complex objectives.

The Prada partnership demonstrates growing collaboration between luxury brands and aerospace companies. Beyond traditional fashion markets, luxury companies are increasingly investing in technical innovation and advanced materials science. For NASA, working with companies outside the traditional aerospace sector provides access to different manufacturing techniques and design approaches that could enhance space mission capabilities.

Following the 2028 Artemis IV landing, NASA plans to conduct a second landing mission, Artemis V, and aims to execute additional moon missions annually thereafter. The long-term goal is to establish a sustained human presence on the lunar surface that will support future exploration goals, including eventual missions to Mars.

The collaboration between Prada and NASA highlights how space exploration is becoming an increasingly collaborative effort between government agencies and private sector innovators.

cards.headline: Researchers find fan-shaped geological structure beneath East Antarctica ice
cards.teaser: Scientists detected a large geological formation under the East Antarctic ice sheet formed by ancient tectonic activity.
cards.body:
Scientists have detected a massive fan-shaped subglacial basin province beneath the East Antarctica ice sheet. The formation was created through rotational extension, a tectonic process that altered Earth's crust over millions of years.

This discovery advances understanding of Antarctica's geological history and the forces that shaped the continent before ice coverage. Researchers used advanced detection methods to map the structure's shape and extent in this remote, ice-covered region.

cards.headline: Australian Aboriginal oral stories may preserve memories from over 10,000 years ago
cards.teaser: Researchers believe some Indigenous Australian stories describe coastlines that disappeared beneath rising seas after the last ice age.
cards.body:
Some Aboriginal Australian oral traditions may contain memories of coastlines that existed more than 10,000 years ago, before rising sea levels submerged them at the end of the last ice age. Researchers examining these stories suggest they could represent some of the oldest surviving true accounts in human history.

The stories describe geographic features and landscapes that match what scientists know about the Australian coastline before it was altered by post-glacial sea level rise. The finding highlights the potential longevity and accuracy of oral storytelling traditions passed down through generations over millennia.

cards.headline: Atlus announces Persona 6 at Xbox Games Showcase
cards.teaser: The next entry in the Persona video game series was revealed with a toxic green color scheme and graveyard visual theme.
cards.body:
Atlus confirmed the existence of Persona 6 during the Xbox Games Showcase 2026 at Summer Game Fest. The announcement came as part of a strong showing for Japanese RPGs at the event, following the reveal of Final Fantasy VII's trilogy conclusion.

The studio released a brief teaser for the game but kept additional details under wraps. The announcement marks the long-awaited return of the Persona series.

cards.headline: Sega confirms use of generative AI in new Crazy Taxi game
cards.teaser: The publisher acknowledged including AI-generated content in Crazy Taxi World Tour, set to release in 2027.
cards.body:
Sega confirmed that the upcoming Crazy Taxi World Tour contains generative AI content and issued a response addressing the decision. The game will reboot the Crazy Taxi series after a lengthy hiatus, with a planned release in 2027 for Xbox and other platforms.

The announcement sparked questions about the role of generative AI in game development. Crazy Taxi World Tour represents the return of the arcade racing series that has been dormant for approximately 20 years. Sega revealed the game at the Xbox showcase alongside details about its gameplay approach.

cards.headline: Halo: Campaign Evolved launches July 28 with new space combat missions
cards.teaser: The latest Halo title introduces space-based combat and will release across Xbox, PlayStation 5, and PC platforms.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced Halo: Campaign Evolved during its Xbox Games Showcase, revealing a July 28 release date across Xbox Series S/X, PC, and PlayStation 5. The remake reimagines Halo: Combat Evolved's campaign with new content, including Operation: Meteorite, a three-mission addition showcased in a recently released trailer.

Pre-orders for the game are now available, with a collector's edition featuring a statue offered alongside the standard release.

cards.headline: Spyro returns with dragon flight feature in spring 2027 game
cards.teaser: A new Spyro game will introduce full dragon flight mechanics for the first time in the franchise's history.
cards.body:
Toys for Bob is developing Spyro: A Realm Beyond, the franchise's first original title since 2008. The game launches spring 2027 across Xbox, PlayStation 5, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2. Tom Kenny returns as the voice of the redesigned purple dragon, staying true to the character's iconic look.

Flight mechanics form the core of the new gameplay. Creative director Lou Studdert explains that players can take to the air at any time, using diving to build speed and fire-breath to ignite campfires that create updrafts for lift. The design emphasizes player agency in how they navigate and interact with the world as a dragon.

hero.headline: Poston wins Memorial in playoff after marathon final round
hero.body:
J.T. Poston captured the Memorial tournament after a playoff with Ryan Gerard that concluded a marathon final day of golf. Poston made a 7-foot birdie putt on the 18th hole to shoot an even-par 72 and force extra holes, then secured victory when Gerard missed a 6-foot par putt on the second playoff hole.

The tournament finish capped an extended day of competition that saw Poston struggle through the regulation round before salvaging a tie with his late birdie. The even-par score kept him level with Gerard heading into the playoff format.

The Memorial, held annually at Muirfield Village Golf Club, represents one of the PGA Tour's signature events. Poston's victory marks a significant achievement in the tournament's storied history, which has featured winners including Tiger Woods and Jack Nicklaus, the tournament's founder and host.

Gerard's missed putt on the second extra hole proved decisive after both players navigated the first playoff hole without separation. The playoff format continued until one player emerged with a clear advantage, with Poston ultimately prevailing when his opponent failed to convert the short par attempt.

The win adds another title to Poston's professional career and solidifies his standing among the tour's competitive field. The marathon day tested both players' endurance and mental fortitude, with Poston's ability to recover from his regulation-round struggles proving crucial to his eventual triumph.

cards.headline: Hamlin claims third win of season at Michigan
cards.teaser: Denny Hamlin earned his third victory of 2026 at Michigan International Speedway despite early damage to his car.
cards.body:
Denny Hamlin rallied to win the NASCAR Cup Series race at Michigan International Speedway, securing his third victory of the 2026 season. Hamlin captured the pole position before the race but his car suffered damage during the event.

The win continues Hamlin's dominance at the Michigan track, where he has consistently performed well throughout his career. His ability to overcome the car damage and work his way back to the front of the field highlighted his driving skill and the team's adjustments during the race.

cards.headline: Skubal throws five scoreless innings in rehab start
cards.teaser: Tigers pitcher Tarik Skubal pitched five scoreless innings in his first rehab start, just one month after elbow surgery.
cards.body:
Tarik Skubal looked dominant in his rehabilitation start, throwing five scoreless innings in his first outing since undergoing a new elbow procedure. The Tigers' Cy Young winner had surgery just four weeks earlier and made the rehab appearance as part of his recovery process.

Skubal's performance suggests a potentially quick return to the Tigers' rotation. The pitcher underwent the procedure to repair his elbow using a new surgical technique, and his strong showing in the rehab start indicates positive progress in his recovery timeline.

cards.headline: Chisholm hits three-run homer with Judge's bat in Yankees win
cards.teaser: Jazz Chisholm Jr. borrowed Aaron Judge's bat and hit a three-run home run to cap a five-run eighth inning in the Yankees' victory at Boston.
cards.body:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. borrowed Aaron Judge's bat and made it count in a big way. After struggling early in the game, Chisholm used the injured captain's lumber to launch a three-run homer that capped off a five-run eighth inning rally Sunday against Boston.

The home run proved pivotal in the Yankees' comeback victory. With Judge sidelined, Chisholm found a creative way to keep the captain's presence felt in the lineup, delivering the offensive spark needed to secure the win over the Red Sox.

cards.headline: Spurs remain confident despite 2-0 Finals deficit
cards.teaser: Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs say they remain confident in their chances despite trailing the Knicks 2-0 in the NBA Finals.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama says he is embracing both the setbacks and success as the San Antonio Spurs prepare for Game 3 of the NBA Finals against the New York Knicks on Monday at Madison Square Garden. Down 2-0 in the series, Wembanyama emphasizes the importance of acceptance and reflecting on the team's journey so far.

The Spurs star remains undaunted by the deficit heading into the hostile environment at Madison Square Garden. Wembanyama believes this moment is what he was built for as San Antonio looks to mount a comeback in the best-of-seven series.

cards.headline: Blue Jays win after disputed baseline call against Orioles
cards.teaser: Ernie Clement was ruled safe despite Baltimore's belief he left the baseline, helping Toronto secure a 6-4 victory.
cards.body:
Ernie Clement was ruled safe after dodging a tag attempt by Baltimore Orioles shortstop Gunnar Henderson during Toronto's 6-4 victory. Clement swerved to his right to evade the play, and Henderson threw to first base expecting him to be called out for leaving the baseline.

The Orioles disputed the ruling, believing Clement had strayed too far from the baseline and should have been ruled out. Despite their objection, the umpires allowed the safe call to stand, a decision that proved significant in the Blue Jays' win.

cards.headline: Eriksen collapses during Denmark friendly, reported conscious
cards.teaser: Christian Eriksen collapsed on the pitch during a friendly between Denmark and Ukraine, with officials saying he was conscious afterward.
cards.body:
Christian Eriksen collapsed on the pitch during a Denmark friendly against Ukraine on Sunday. The midfielder, a former Tottenham and Manchester United player, was quickly attended to by medical personnel in Odense.

The Danish Football Association confirmed that Eriksen was conscious after the incident. The match was abandoned and not resumed following the collapse.

hero.headline: Backrooms Becomes A24's Highest-Grossing Film Ever at $212 Million Worldwide
hero.body:
A24's horror film Backrooms has surpassed $212 million at the worldwide box office, making it the independent studio's highest-grossing movie ever. The film has overtaken Timothée Chalamet's Marty Supreme to claim the top spot in the company's history.

The internet-based horror concept has resonated strongly with younger audiences. Multiple sources report that Generation Z viewers are driving the film's success, with some suggesting the genre offers an escape from contemporary pressures. The movie adapts the popular online horror concept that emerged from YouTube and other digital platforms before transitioning to the big screen.

Producer Peter Chernin has commented on what the film's breakthrough means for the entertainment industry's future direction. The project signals a departure from the superhero-dominated franchises that have controlled box office performance in recent years. Industry analysts view the film as evidence that horror concepts originating in internet culture can achieve mainstream theatrical success and compete with major franchise releases.

The Backrooms concept centers on the idea of infinite empty rooms and liminal spaces. Its evolution from user-generated online content to record-breaking theatrical release represents a significant shift in how digital culture influences traditional entertainment. The film's performance vastly exceeds typical independent releases, demonstrating that A24's previous box office records pale in comparison to this achievement.

The success arrives during a period when major Hollywood studios are reevaluating their content strategies. After years of superhero saturation, Backrooms provides a case study in how original horror concepts with established online audiences can draw audiences comparable to major tentpole releases. The film's strong international performance suggests appeal that extends well beyond the core internet fanbase that initially embraced the concept.

This development reflects broader industry trends. Entertainment observers note that audiences appear increasingly interested in alternatives to franchise-based content. The Backrooms phenomenon demonstrates that properties born from digital platforms can translate successfully to traditional theatrical releases when marketed effectively to their existing communities.

The film's trajectory offers lessons for studios considering how to develop internet-native properties. Rather than dismissing viral online concepts as niche curiosities, the commercial success of Backrooms suggests studios should actively pursue digital content with demonstrated audience enthusiasm. The transition from YouTube phenomenon to box office record holder indicates a viable path forward as streaming platforms and social media continue shaping entertainment consumption patterns.

A24's record-breaking performance with Backrooms marks a pivotal moment in how independent studios approach content acquisition and development, particularly regarding properties with built-in digital audiences ready to support theatrical releases.

cards.headline: 79th Annual Tony Awards Ceremony Underway
cards.teaser: Broadway's biggest night is taking place with four productions competing for top honors.
cards.body:
Broadway's biggest night is happening now, with the 79th Tony Awards ceremony kicking off at 8 p.m. ET. Multiple outlets are providing live coverage as winners are announced throughout the evening.

Four major productions are among the leading contenders: The Lost Boys, a punk-rock vampire adaptation; Schmigadoon!, a comedic tribute to Golden Age musicals; a production about a salesman; and a show featuring fierce feline ballroom dancers. The ceremony honors the best of Broadway's current season across multiple categories.

cards.headline: Lawsuit Filed to Block UFC Event Planned for White House South Lawn
cards.teaser: Two Virginia residents are seeking to stop a UFC fight scheduled as part of America's 250th birthday celebration.
cards.body:
Two Virginia residents have filed a federal lawsuit to stop a UFC fight card scheduled for the White House South Lawn. The event, dubbed UFC Freedom 250, is being held in conjunction with President Trump's 80th birthday and as part of the nation's 250th anniversary celebrations.

The lawsuit targets the National Park Service and Department of the Interior, the agencies responsible for managing White House grounds. The legal challenge seeks to prevent the mixed martial arts competition from taking place at this unconventional venue.

cards.headline: Scott Pelley Discusses Bari Weiss Era and Final Days at 60 Minutes
cards.teaser: The former CBS correspondent addressed his departure from the news program in a New York Times profile.
cards.body:
Former CBS News anchor Scott Pelley has accused editorial management of interfering with a broadcast segment about the killing of Minneapolis protester Renee Good by an immigration officer. Pelley claims that Bari Weiss, CBS News's editor-in-chief, sent an email to his supervisor requesting changes to the report before it aired. According to Pelley, Weiss wanted the segment to state that Good was driving toward an officer.

The veteran broadcaster was recently dismissed from 60 Minutes. His dismissal has drawn criticism from prominent figures including Sarah Safer, daughter of legendary correspondent Morley Safer, who expressed concern about editorial interference at the program. Three other 60 Minutes correspondents—Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker, and Jon Wertheim—have indicated they will remain with the show.

cards.headline: FCC Chairman Criticizes Scott Pelley Over 60 Minutes Firing Comments
cards.teaser: Brendan Carr called the journalist completely out of touch for claiming his firing was a surprise.
cards.body:
Scott Pelley, recently fired from CBS News, has accused the network's new leadership of interfering with his reporting. Pelley claims CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss pressured him to alter a segment about an immigration officer's killing of Minneapolis protester Renee Good, and says executives instructed him to "inject falsehoods and bias" into his work.

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr responded by criticizing Pelley for stating in a New York Times profile that he had not anticipated being fired. Carr argued that legacy journalists being out of touch with reality is part of why public trust in traditional media remains low.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Opens Eternal Sunshine Tour in Oakland
cards.teaser: The singer performed the first show of her new tour at Oakland Arena.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande opened her Eternal Sunshine Tour with a performance at Oakland Arena on Saturday night. The show demonstrated her impressive vocal range and served as the first stop on the extended tour run.

The concert was built around the concept of her Eternal Sunshine album, bringing the project's themes to life on stage for her audience.

cards.headline: Bob Dylan Performs You Ain't Goin' Nowhere for First Time in 14 Years
cards.teaser: The musician played the Basement Tapes song in concert after more than a decade.
cards.body:
Bob Dylan performed the song You Ain't Goin' Nowhere for the first time in 14 years during a recent concert. The track comes from the Basement Tapes recording sessions and had not been part of Dylan's live repertoire since 2012.

The performance came two days after Dylan played Baby, Won't You Be My Baby for the first time since recording it 59 years ago. Both songs represent deep cuts from Dylan's extensive catalog of material from the Basement Tapes sessions. The back-to-back rare performances mark an unusual approach to setlist selection during the current tour.

hero.headline: Maine Democrats threaten electoral vote change if Nebraska acts
hero.teaser: Democratic gubernatorial candidates say they would support winner-take-all system in response to potential Nebraska changes.
hero.body:
Democrats in Maine are threatening to change how the state awards Electoral College votes if Republican-led Nebraska modifies its system for the 2028 presidential election. Several Democrats running to be Maine's next governor have signaled they would support adopting a winner-take-all electoral vote system if Nebraska makes similar changes.

The dispute represents the latest example of partisan election politics that could influence the outcome of the 2028 presidential race. Both Maine and Nebraska currently split their electoral votes, unlike most states. Any changes to how either state allocates votes could affect the electoral math in a close presidential contest.

cards.headline: Lawsuit challenges UFC fight planned for White House lawn
cards.teaser: A legal filing seeks to halt a UFC event scheduled for June 14 on the White House South Lawn for Trump's birthday.
cards.body:
A federal lawsuit seeks to halt a UFC fight card scheduled for the White House South Lawn on June 14, President Trump's 80th birthday. The legal challenge contends that the Trump administration's authorization of the event was unlawful.

The mixed martial arts spectacle is being promoted as part of celebrations marking the nation's 250th anniversary.

cards.headline: Bolton warns Trump's Iran policy risks nuclear proliferation
cards.teaser: Former national security adviser says administration decisions during conflict have laid groundwork for arms race.
cards.body:
Former national security adviser John Bolton warned Sunday that President Trump's actions in the war against Iran could spark a nuclear arms race in the Middle East. Bolton made the assessment in an opinion piece published Sunday.

Bolton argued that regardless of any deal Trump reaches with Iran, the president's decisions during the conflict have created conditions for increased nuclear proliferation in the region. He characterized Trump's approach as contradictory and warned of long-term consequences for regional security.

cards.headline: Trump urges Netanyahu not to retaliate after Iranian missile strike
cards.teaser: President Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday not to retaliate against Iran's missile attack and to allow more time for diplomacy, ac.
cards.body:
President Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday not to retaliate against Iran's missile attack and to allow more time for diplomacy, according to a senior U.S. official and an Israeli source familiar with the call. The conversation took place after Iran launched ballistic missiles at northern Israel on Sunday night, the first such strike in two months.

Trump's intervention signals the administration's effort to prevent escalating tensions between Israel and Iran from undermining ongoing U.S. negotiations with Tehran. Before the call, Trump told reporters he planned to urge Netanyahu to hold off on any military response. A U.S. official confirmed that Trump has been briefed on the Iranian missile attack.

The missile strike threatened to derail a fragile ceasefire that had held between the U.S. and Iran. The Israeli Defense Forces posted about the attack on social media, confirming that Iran had launched ballistic missiles targeting northern Israel. The incident marked Tehran's first direct strike on Israel since the ceasefire took effect two months ago.

The Trump administration has been working to negotiate with Iran even as the U.S. remains engaged in military operations against the country. The president has faced criticism over his Iran policy, with some observers questioning whether the conflict contradicts his 2024 campaign promise of no new wars. Trump has rejected that characterization, dismissing suggestions that launching military action against Iran betrayed his campaign messaging.

The situation presents a diplomatic challenge for the administration as it attempts to balance its relationship with Israel, manage tensions with Iran, and advance negotiations. Former national security adviser John Bolton warned in an opinion piece that Trump's actions in the conflict with Iran could spark a nuclear arms race in the Middle East, regardless of any eventual deal. The administration now faces the task of preventing further escalation while continuing diplomatic efforts with Tehran.

cards.headline: Trump dismisses criticism over 'no new wars' campaign pledge
cards.teaser: President rejects suggestion that Iran conflict contradicts his 2024 campaign messaging.
cards.body:
President Trump dismissed criticism that military action against Iran contradicts his 2024 campaign pledge of "no new wars." The president addressed the apparent conflict between his campaign messaging and the current conflict with Iran during recent remarks.

Trump rejected the characterization that launching military action against Iran represents a betrayal of his campaign promise. Critics have pointed to the Iran conflict as evidence that contradicts his stated commitment to avoiding new wars while running for office.

cards.headline: Jewish Democrats voice concerns about party antisemitism ahead of 2028
cards.teaser: Growing number of Jewish party members warn hostilities over Israel could hurt Democrats in swing states.
cards.body:
A growing number of Jewish Democrats say they feel shunned within their own party, warning that escalating hostilities over Israel's actions in Gaza have at times crossed into hostility toward Jewish Americans. The concerns come as party members look ahead to the 2028 election.

Those raising alarms say the constant tensions could hurt Democrats in the next presidential race, particularly in swing states such as Pennsylvania, Michigan and Georgia, which have large Jewish populations. A large majority of Jewish Americans traditionally vote Democratic, and any shifts among Jewish voters who feel alienated could impact electoral outcomes in competitive states.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Biden cabinet member could become first female Native American governor if elected.
cards.body:
Former Biden administration official Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor on Sunday. Haaland previously served as Interior Secretary in the Biden cabinet.

If elected in the general election, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor. She will face the Republican nominee in the race to lead New Mexico.
